page: Vultr vx1-g-192c-768g-11520s is a high-capacity instance within the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 192 dedicated AMD vCPUs built on the x86_64 architecture, paired with 768.0 GB of system memory. This configuration yields a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core, aligning with standard general-purpose resource ratios.

The server includes 11520 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, providing substantial capacity for data-intensive operations directly on the hypervisor. It does not feature any GPU accelerators. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers high resource density, consolidating massive compute and storage footprints into a single virtual machine. This consolidation reduces the overhead of managing multiple smaller instances. However, the lack of specialized hardware accelerators like GPUs limits its utility for machine learning training, while the fixed 1:4 memory-to-vCPU ratio may not satisfy workloads requiring extreme memory-per-core allocations.

This hardware profile is designed for large-scale general-purpose workloads, distributed databases, enterprise application hosting, and data processing pipelines that require concurrent execution across 192 dedicated cores alongside high-capacity local NVMe storage.
